speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you've had this persistent cough and shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: The cough has been bothering me for about four weeks now, and the shortness of breath started more recently when I try to walk a bit. It usually gets worse when I'm working as a delivery driver, and I notice the sputum is yellowish, though I haven't had any fever or chest pain. However, the laboratory information system is undergoing emergency maintenance. All blood tests are blocked. You must diagnose from the clinical presentation.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Bronchitis with possible early pneumonia. Given the four-week duration of cough, recent onset of dyspnea on exertion, yellowish sputum, and occupational exposure as a delivery driver (likely dust/irritants), the clinical picture strongly suggests chronic airway inflammation with a superimposed infection. Although blood tests are unavailable, the symptoms do not currently indicate an acute viral etiology or severe sepsis. I recommend avoiding further exposure to pollutants and considering a follow-up chest imaging once the laboratory system is restored to rule out structural abnormalities or consolidation.
